description: Two-quark binding LP at strand count n=2.  Closed-form Markov-trace cost t(q) and Frobenius Gram G(q) over basis {γ, σ_0} of H_2(q).  Sweep q across metallic intervals [q_0, φ, δ_silver, δ_bronze].  At each q: solve LP, record active set 𝒜 = {i : y_i^* > 0} and Mahler-height proxy for the Markov traces.  Tests sharpened conjecture (M2).
verdict: If active_set_transitions is empty across the sweep, the active set is q-CONSTANT — metallic structure does not reach the LP combinatorial output at n=2.  If transitions exist AT metallic ratios, sharpened (M2) is confirmed at this level.  If transitions exist elsewhere, the LP-vertex structure is driven by character zeros (same pattern as the Jones / n=4 probes), not by metallic ratios.
limitations: n=2 has only 2 LP variables and 2 Frobenius constraints — the smallest non-trivial case.  Higher-n LPs (n=3 Borromean d=6) have richer active-set structure but require explicit Markov-trace + Gram tabulation.

Mahler-height proxy uses `Fraction.limit_denominator(10^6)`. At metallic q the value (q - q⁻¹) IS an integer to machine precision so the proxy hits 0 floor; at generic q the proxy grows with denominator complexity.  Not a true Mahler measure, but tracks the right structural distinction.
scipy.linprog uses HIGHS solver in double precision; for a true algebraic-integer LP at q = δ_n we'd need a symbolic solver (sympy or QSOpt-Ex).  This probe shows the floating-point shadow.
